keys.statement: A classic sequencing heuristic, reported by the authors, leaves the most difficult split to last because it needs a high reflux ratio.

plain.title: Classic sequencing rule: leave the hardest split to last
plain.when: You choose the order of splits in a distillation sequence.
plain.do: Leave the most difficult split to last.
plain.why: A difficult split needs a high reflux ratio, which is cheaper with fewer components present.
plain.check: Li et al. 2023 report this classic rule and then qualify it: compare sequences quantitatively.

decisions.mechanism: A difficult split needs high reflux, cheaper with fewer components present.
decisions.expected_change: Lower energy for the difficult split.
limits: Reported by Li et al. as a classic heuristic, which they then qualify (see the disputed row).

keys.statement: The authors find the hardest split can also pay early, and that non-key components present during a difficult split inflate the column flows; the balance depends on the case, so sequences should be compared by optimisation.

plain.title: The hardest split can also pay early: compare sequences by optimisation
plain.when: You choose the order of splits in a distillation sequence.
plain.do: Compare sequences quantitatively, by optimisation, rather than by a fixed rule.
plain.why: Two effects oppose: the high reflux of a difficult split, and the non-key components present during it, which inflate the column flows. Li et al. 2023 find the balance depends on the case.
plain.check: Screen with shortcut models plus heat integration, then simulate the best few rigorously.

decisions.mechanism: Opposing effects of reflux and of non-key components on flows.
decisions.expected_change: The sequence that is actually cheapest.

keys.statement: Choose column pressure so the condenser can use cooling water rather than refrigeration, and set it together with heat integration.

plain.title: Choose column pressure so the condenser can use cooling water
plain.when: A column's condenser temperature would need refrigeration.
plain.do: Raise the column pressure until the condenser can use cooling water, and set it together with the heat integration.
plain.why: Higher pressure raises the condensing temperature.
plain.check: In CHEPTA, scan the pressure and record condenser and reboiler temperatures against your utilities.

decisions.obstacle: A low condenser temperature needs refrigeration.
decisions.mechanism: Higher pressure raises the condensing temperature.
decisions.operation: Raise pressure to the cooling-water level.

keys.statement: Shortcut column models (Fenske-Underwood-Gilliland) combined with heat-exchanger network synthesis screened distillation sequences reliably; only the best few needed rigorous simulation.

plain.title: Many sequences to compare: screen with shortcut models and heat integration, simulate only the best few
plain.when: There are too many distillation sequences to simulate rigorously.
plain.do: Screen with shortcut column models (Fenske-Underwood-Gilliland) combined with heat-exchanger network synthesis, and simulate only the best few rigorously.
plain.why: For zeotropic mixtures (no azeotropes) shortcuts rank sequences as rigorous models do.
plain.check: Li et al. 2023 showed this for zeotropic hydrocarbons only: do not rely on it for azeotropic mixtures without a rigorous check.

decisions.obstacle: Too many sequences to simulate rigorously.
decisions.mechanism: Shortcuts rank sequences as rigorous models do for zeotropic mixtures.
decisions.operation: Screen with shortcuts, verify the best rigorously.

keys.statement: Without heat integration, thermally coupled complex columns beat sequences of simple columns by a wide margin; once heat integration is included the difference narrows a lot.

plain.title: Thermally coupled columns against simple ones: compare with heat integration included
plain.when: You choose between thermally coupled complex columns and sequences of simple columns.
plain.do: Include heat integration in both options before comparing them.
plain.why: Without heat integration coupled columns win by a wide margin; heat integration recovers much of what coupling saves, so the gap narrows a lot.
plain.check: Run the pinch targets for both options.

decisions.obstacle: Choosing between complex and simple columns.
decisions.mechanism: Heat integration recovers much of what coupling saves.
decisions.operation: Compare complex and simple columns with heat integration included.
